_comment: When a notated item provides a demand at a useful density, not only somewhere in the file (E0, 2026-09-27).
The app's detectors (app/src/demands/detect.ts) say whether a demand is present and where: each located
place is one note, step or interval, counted in `measurement.located`. Presence is not an opportunity: two
skips in forty bars are in the piece, and a learner who plays it has not practised skips. So an item
establishes a demand when the located count reaches `min` AND the count per bar reaches `perBar`. Both,
because a long piece passes a count by accident and a short one cannot reach a count at all.
One rule per demand, never one universal percentage (Part 15 §13, D0). Each is a hypothesis, marked as
such, with its reason: a teacher's reading of how often a thing has to come back before playing the piece
practises it. They are the builder's (E0) and a reviewer may set them otherwise; the rung-claims report
(docs/prompts/rung-claims.md) is where a threshold that refuses a good piece would show.
A generated item may also establish a demand by its own family contract (tools/content/family_contracts.json),
where the contract states a density for it (a count of two or more, or a count per bar) and the item meets
it: the family's threshold is its own considered one, and a four-bar drill cannot reach a whole-piece count.
A contract that asks only for presence (a count of one, or none) states no density, and the rule here
decides — which is how the tie drill's one tie in four bars is not taken as adequate practice (D0's
reviewer, finding 6).
An excerpt (E1, docs/03 §4c) is judged by the window rule: `perBar` reached and at least `minInWindow`, the
count a four-to-eight-bar passage has to reach, in place of `min` (a whole-piece count a short cut cannot
hold is the file's own point). Each is a hypothesis with its reason (`windowWhy`), never above `min`, read by
the build's `attach_demands` for an excerpt and by the proposer (tools/content/excerpt_proposer.py) for a
window; a threshold met is never proof of teaching quality, and the proposer reports every window it refuses.
`tempoSensitive`: what the learner has to cope with depends on how fast it goes, not only on whether it is
written (notes shorter than the beat, at the tempo the piece is played). Where a piece's tempo is the
converter's default rather than written (the `tempo-defaulted` tag; a converted edition with no tempo of
its own), these demands are measured in the notation and their difficulty is not: the provenance marks
them untrusted (R11, Part 12 §13).
Read by the build (tools/content/build.py, which writes `measurement.established` on every bundled item)
and by the app (app/src/curriculum/eligibility.ts, which applies the same rule to an imported score).
app/tests/unit/eligibility.test.ts holds the two readings equal on every item of the built catalog.
`curatedOnly` (CD1, the brief's §3a after docs/review/responses/33497357.md §2): demands with no general
density rule, by decision. Their detectors are exact presence and location facts; no count of located places
makes an item establish them. They are established by two proofs only: a generated family's contract
(build.established_by_contract, once the independent witness agrees) and a verified passage fact
(the `demand` rows of content/sources/verified-facts.json, tools/content/passages.py) for the exact item, rung and bars it proves.
Every vocabulary demand is in exactly one of `demands` and `curatedOnly`. No sentinel threshold, no hypothesis.

clef.bass.windowWhy: a bass-staff note in every bar of a four-bar phrase; the whole piece's eight is two phrases
clef.bass.why: reading the bass staff is practised when it carries notes throughout; a bass note under the last chord is not bass-clef reading

pitch.ledger.windowWhy: two ledger-line notes read in a short passage; one is incidental
pitch.ledger.why: ledger-line notes are sparse by nature; four in a piece are read more than once, one in forty bars is incidental

interval.step.windowWhy: a step in every bar of a four-bar phrase
interval.step.why: steps are the commonest interval; a piece practises reading them when most bars have one

interval.skip.windowWhy: a passage offered for skips reads one three times; two is a pair
interval.skip.why: a skip in every other bar and half a dozen in all makes the skip a habit to read, not an event

interval.leap.windowWhy: a passage offered for leaps brings the leap back three times; two is a pair, one an event
interval.leap.why: a leap once a phrase (every four bars) and four in all; a single octave leap at the end is incidental

rhythm.eighths.windowWhy: two pairs of eighths: the division comes back inside the passage
rhythm.eighths.why: counting eighths is practised when pairs of them come back in half the bars; one pickup pair is not

rhythm.shorter-than-quarter.windowWhy: as eighths: two divided beats at least
rhythm.shorter-than-quarter.why: as eighths: the division of the beat has to recur to be practised

rhythm.sixteenths.why: a group of four at least every four bars and two groups in all

rhythm.dotted-quarter.windowWhy: the figure twice in the passage
rhythm.dotted-quarter.why: the figure once a phrase: four in a sixteen-bar tune, one in a whole piece is incidental

rhythm.ties.windowWhy: two ties; the tie drill's one tie in four bars stays below it (D0 finding 6)
rhythm.ties.why: a tie once a phrase and four in all; the tie drill's one tie in four bars does not reach it (D0 finding 6)

rhythm.syncopation.windowWhy: three syncopated notes: the figure recurs inside the passage, not one off-beat entry
rhythm.syncopation.why: a syncopated note once a phrase and four in all; a single off-beat entry is not a syncopated piece

rhythm.triplets.windowWhy: one triplet group (each triplet note is located)
rhythm.triplets.why: each triplet note is located, so six is two groups; at least one group every four bars

metre.compound.windowWhy: compound time in whole bars: every note in them is located, so four bars of two beats reach it and a stray bar does not
metre.compound.why: compound time is a property of whole bars; every note in them is located, so a few bars of 6/8 in a 4/4 piece do not make it practice in 6/8

key.signature.windowWhy: the letters the signature alters sound at least four times
key.signature.why: the signature is practised when the letters it alters sound often: in half the bars at least

pitch.chromatic.windowWhy: three notes outside the key: accidentals are occasional, and one or two in a short passage are colour, not practice
pitch.chromatic.why: accidentals are occasional by nature; four read in a piece, one in forty bars is incidental

range.beyond-position.windowWhy: as the whole piece: two notes that take a hand past a fifth is a hand that has to move
range.beyond-position.why: the detector locates each note that widens a hand past a fifth, which a piece does a few times however long it is; two is a hand that has to move, one may be a final note

texture.hands-together.windowWhy: the hands coordinated in at least four places
texture.hands-together.why: located only where the hands are coordinated; in half the bars at least, or the texture is a moment and not the piece

texture.left-hand-pattern.windowWhy: the every-bar rule, read on the cut: present means a pattern in every bar of the passage
texture.left-hand-pattern.why: the detector is already an every-bar rule: present means a pattern in every bar

texture.walking-bass.windowWhy: the every-bar rule, read on the cut: present means a walk in every bar of the passage (E22's caution stands)
texture.walking-bass.why: the detector is already an every-bar rule: present means a walk in every bar (and its readings are known to misread a stride left hand and a one-line pulse, E22)

rhythm.habanera.why: No general rule (CD1 §3a): the habanera is the left hand's onset cell, a presence and location fact; the density numbers were measured through the hand model HD2 corrects and no named consumer needs a general rule. Established only by a verified passage fact (Bizet bars 1-12, Por Una Cabeza printed bars 1-14) or a family contract with the witness agreeing. A later named consumer with a predeclared calibration that separates its cases may add a rule then.

rhythm.tresillo.why: No general rule (CD1; docs/review/responses/33497357.md §2): the predeclared calibration falsified one (docs/prompts/runs/CD1/calibration.md): the strictest min-and-perBar rule keeping The Crave also establishes the counterexample All of Me. Established only by the tresillo family's contract (exercise.tresillo.c/.f/.g, the witness agreeing) or a verified passage fact (The Crave bars 21-26).

metre.three-four.why: No general rule (SR2; the orchestrator's decision under the reviewer's ruling on SR1, docs/review/responses/sr1-sightreading-quality.md §3): no named consumer needs one, and a rule chosen so that 1.4's four-bar waltz drills pass would be calibrated on the very case it judges (metre.compound's 16 and 1 a bar establish 227 of the 237 items that locate 3/4 and none of 1.4's three drills). Established only by a family contract: the rhythm family's waltz patterns require it in every bar, the app's detector located and partitura's time signatures agreeing on every catalogue file (SR2 H7).
